title: Opposite reversal of joins and internal functor simplicial sets
statement:
Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], opposite simplicial sets as defined in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], and the left join and fat left cone of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. Let $K,S$ be small simplicial sets and $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe. Define $K\star\Delta^0$ by ordered blocks of $K$-vertices followed by vertices at a new final vertex. There are natural simplicial isomorphisms
$$(K\star\Delta^0)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad \operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The first reverses the ordered join blocks. In degree $n$, the second sends $h:S\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ to $h^{\mathrm{op}}:S^{\mathrm{op}}\times(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, using the vertex-reversal identification $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^n$. They commute with restriction along every simplicial map of shapes, in particular $K\hookrightarrow K\star\Delta^0$, and with evaluation at the apex. Let $u_K:K\times\Delta^1\to K\star\Delta^0$ split each interval simplex into its initial $0$-vertices in $K$ and final $1$-vertices at the apex. After reversal of $K$, the parameter simplices and the interval, $u_K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the map $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}}$ collapsing the initial $0$-vertices to the apex and retaining the final $1$-vertices in $K^{\mathrm{op}}$, namely the map factoring through the fat left cone in that node.

proof.text: Write $r_n(i)=n-i$ and $\alpha^\vee=r_n\alpha r_m$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] says $X^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=X(\alpha^\vee)$. Since $r_n^2=1$, we have $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$ and $(\alpha\beta)^\vee=\alpha^\vee\beta^\vee$. Products are degreewise by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so $(X\times Y)^{\mathrm{op}}=X^{\mathrm{op}}\times Y^{\mathrm{op}}$. The map $j_n:(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^n$ sends $t:[m]\to[n]$ to $t^\vee=r_nt r_m$. It is simplicial because $(t\alpha^\vee)^\vee=t^\vee\alpha$, and its inverse has the identical formula. These are literal identities of functions; no reversal $r_n$ is being treated as a monotone simplex operator.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $K\star\Delta^0$ is specified by a cut $p\in\{0,\ldots,n+1\}$, the number of initial $K$-vertices, and, when $p>0$, a simplex $x\in K_{p-1}$; $p=0$ is the unique pure-apex simplex. Define $R_n$ by sending this to a simplex of $\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $n+1-p$ initial apex vertices and final simplex the same $x$, regarded in $K^{\mathrm{op}}_{p-1}$. This uses the ordered-block definition of the left join in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the source operator uses $\alpha^\vee$. Its retained $K$-indices are exactly the reversals of the final indices $i$ with $\alpha(i)\geq n+1-p$ in the target join. On these indices the two restriction maps are related by $r_{p-1}(-)r_{q-1}$, where $q$ is the number retained. Thus the opposite operator on $x$ is exactly the operator of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ on the final block. For $q=0$ both outputs are pure apex. Hence $R$ is simplicial. Reversing the cut and the blocks a second time returns $p,x$, giving its inverse. This argument includes $p=n+1$ (pure $K$) and $K=\varnothing$.

proof.text:
For an $n$-simplex $h:S\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ of the opposite functor simplicial set, define $\Phi_n(h):S^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $\Phi_n(h)_m(s,t)=h_m(s,t^\vee)$, using equality of the underlying degreewise sets. Here $s\in S_m$ and $t:[m]\to[n]$. For $\gamma:[l]\to[m]$, simpliciality of $h$ gives
$$\mathcal E(\gamma^\vee)h_m(s,t^\vee)=h_l(S(\gamma^\vee)s,t^\vee\gamma^\vee)=h_l(S^{\mathrm{op}}(\gamma)s,(t\gamma)^\vee).$$
This is precisely the required simpliciality equation for $\Phi_n(h)$, using the internal functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the opposite definition of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Equivalently $\Phi_n(h)$ is $h^{\mathrm{op}}$ precomposed with $1\times j_n^{-1}$.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the operator in $\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ takes $h$ to $h\circ(1\times\Delta(\alpha^\vee))$, by the two cited definitions. For an $l$-simplex $(s,t)$, $t:[l]\to[m]$, its image under $\Phi_m$ is $h_l(s,\alpha^\vee t^\vee)=h_l(s,(\alpha t)^\vee)$, exactly the value of $\Phi_n(h)\circ(1\times\Delta(\alpha))$. Thus $\Phi$ commutes with every parameter operator. Apply the construction again with $S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$: the value becomes $h_l(s,(t^\vee)^\vee)=h_l(s,t)$. Reversal twice is the identity, so this gives a degreewise inverse and hence the claimed simplicial isomorphism. Quasicategory axioms are not needed for this calculation.

proof.text: For a simplicial map $a:S'\to S$, the two orders of restriction and $\Phi$ both have value $h_l(a_l(s'),t^\vee)$. For $b:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$, postcomposition in the two orders has value $b_l(h_l(s,t^\vee))$. For $a:K'\to K$, the two orders of joining and $R$ both keep the same cut and replace the retained simplex $x$ by $a(x)$ in the reversed block. In particular $R$ carries the pure-$K$ inclusion to the pure-$K^{\mathrm{op}}$ inclusion and the apex to the apex. Apply the restriction identity for $\Phi$ to these two inclusions: it gives the asserted commuting restriction and evaluation squares on all parameter simplices. This uses evaluation as restriction, as specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; it proves strict commutation, not merely agreement on objects.

proof.text:
Describe $u_K$ in degree $n$ on $(x,\epsilon)$, where $x\in K_n$ and $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$. If $p$ is the number of zeros of $\epsilon$, its image has initial $K$-block $x|_{\{0,\ldots,p-1\}}$ and final apex block. Restrictions commute with this prescription because the zero block of $\epsilon\alpha$ is the inverse image under $\alpha$ of that of $\epsilon$; this also covers the pure-block cases. Under the product identification of step 1 put
$$w=R\circ u_K^{\mathrm{op}}\circ(1\times j_1^{-1}):K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
For $(x,\eta)$ in degree $n$, $j_1^{-1}$ gives $\eta^\vee(i)=1-\eta(n-i)$. Thus the zeros retained by $u_K$ are the reversed final ones of $\eta$. After $R$ they form exactly the final $K^{\mathrm{op}}$-block restricted from $x$ by the opposite operator; the initial zeros of $\eta$ form the apex block. This proves the cylinder identity with its indicated orientation, in every degree. In particular $\eta=0$ gives the apex and $\eta=1$ gives $x$.

proof.text: By the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], $T_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}$ is the degreewise pushout $\Delta^0\amalg_{K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\{0\}}(K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1)$. The map $w$ of step 6 is constant at the apex on the glued zero end. Assign the adjoined point to that apex. These assignments agree on the overlap, so the set-theoretic quotient in each degree defines a map $T_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\to\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}}$; its operators commute since they do on both pieces. The formula in step 6 identifies it with the fat left-cone collapse specified by that node. For $K=\varnothing$ the cylinder is empty but $T_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}=\Delta^0$, and the same apex assignment defines the required factorization. All formulas commute with restriction of $x$ and of interval and parameter simplices, so the cylinder comparison has the same shape naturality and apex compatibility as the preceding isomorphisms.
